summary: Eight selected papers emphasize identified-hadron collectivity and light-nucleus formation at the LHC, fluctuation-aware extraction of QCD thermodynamics, spin-3/2 polarization, nonflow control in light-ion systems, and statistically grounded machine-learning validation and regularization for HEP.
professional_summary: The strongest result is ALICE's identified-hadron elliptic-flow measurement in O-O collisions, where the phi-versus-Lambda comparison disfavors a mass-only explanation of the intermediate-pT splitting. A second ALICE analysis uses antideuteron-net-Lambda correlations to isolate nucleosynthesis effects. Method papers address fluctuation-biased speed-of-sound inference, small-system nonflow, uncertainty-aware generative-model validation, and modal regularization in PDF fits.
strongest_paper_summary: ALICE identified-hadron v2 in O-O: the phi tracks the lighter K0S rather than the similarly massive Lambda, strongly disfavoring a mass-only explanation and supporting partonic hadronization.

papers.title: Evidence of partonic collectivity in OO collisions through the measurement of phi, K0S, and Lambda elliptic flow
papers.author_count_note: ArXiv exposes only the collaboration label; full author list begins on page 17.
papers.abstract: The first identified-hadron v2 measurement in O-O collisions finds low-pT mass ordering and a greater-than-10-sigma baryon-meson splitting at intermediate pT. The phi follows K0S rather than the similarly massive Lambda, supporting recombination from a collectively flowing partonic medium.

papers.title: Measurement of antideuteron and net-Lambda number fluctuations at the Large Hadron Collider
papers.author_count_note: ArXiv exposes only the collaboration label; full author list begins on page 15.
papers.abstract: The first antideuteron-net-Lambda number correlation in Pb-Pb collisions is consistent with statistical hadronization, while antideuteron-antiproton correlations require additional nucleosynthesis effects described through coalescence.

papers.title: Extracting the QCD speed of sound in the presence of quantum fluctuations
papers.short_authors: Yu-Shan Mu, Li Yan, Xu-Guang Huang
papers.abstract: A statistical estimator uses Gaussianity of residual quantum fluctuations to reduce bias in speed-of-sound extraction from mean-pT and multiplicity correlations. Hydrodynamic tests recover lattice-QCD-like values and distinguish a nonthermal transport comparison.

papers.title: Covariant Wigner function and spin polarization of the Rarita-Schwinger field
papers.short_authors: Matteo Buzzegoli, Aleksandar Gecic, Rajeev Singh
papers.abstract: A covariant Wigner-function treatment derives spin-3/2 polarization from vorticity, shear, and spin potential in several pseudo-gauges, proposing local Omega-minus polarization as a discriminator.

papers.title: Improved nonflow control for multiparticle correlators and system-size-dependent evolution from OO to Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC
papers.abstract: Low-multiplicity-anchored nonflow subtraction schemes are tested in a toy model and Pythia 8 Angantyr; the better-closing v1-based scaling is used for AMPT predictions of symmetry-plane correlators and normalized symmetric cumulants in O-O.

papers.title: An end-to-end framework for uncertainty-aware validation of generative models
papers.short_authors: Giada Badaracco, Sean Benevedes, Christina Reissel, Philip Harris, Gaia Grosso
papers.abstract: SIGMA propagates finite-training-sample uncertainty from a Gaussian-mixture density into a composite-null goodness-of-fit test. A collider QCD benchmark remains calibrated for test sets roughly an order of magnitude larger than standard point-null validation permits.

papers.title: The proton structure one mode at a time: a Neural Tangent Kernel analysis of a DIS fit
papers.short_authors: Amedeo Chiefa, Luigi Del Debbio, Richard Kenway
papers.abstract: An exact multiflavor NTK gradient-flow analysis, validated in a realistic DIS PDF fit, shows leading modes reconstructing the target before subleading modes learn data noise and clarifies implicit regularization and training geometry.

papers.title: Regression on high-dimensional phase space
papers.abstract: A large-multiplicity expansion makes regression with energy flow polynomials analytically tractable and proves inverse-multiplicity-squared covariance scaling from symmetry and conservation-law cancellations.
